title.rendered: Little Girl, Arise | Teach Me How to Pray, Day 10

excerpt.rendered: By the time Jesus arrived at Jairus’s house, the twelve-year-old was dead. Jesus put out the mourners, took her by the hand, and spoke two Aramaic words. The dead child sat up.

content.rendered:
By the time Jesus arrived at Jairus’s house, the twelve-year-old girl was already dead. The mourners were wailing. Jesus put them all out of the room, took her by the hand, and spoke two Aramaic words. The dead child sat up.

The Gospel For Today | Monday, October 12, 2026 | Teach Me How to Pray, Day 10

Today’s Scripture

“Then He took the child by the hand, and said to her, ‘Talitha, cumi,’ which is translated, ‘Little girl, I say to you, arise.’ Immediately the girl arose and walked, for she was twelve years of age.”
Mark 5:41-42 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Jairus was one of the rulers of the synagogue in Capernaum. His twelve-year-old daughter was dying. He pushed through the crowd that surrounded Jesus and fell at His feet, begging Him to come lay hands on her. Jesus agreed. They set off together, with the crowd pressing in on all sides. On the way, Jesus was delayed by the woman with the issue of blood. By the time He was ready to continue, messengers arrived from Jairus’s house with the news every father dreads. “Your daughter is dead. Why trouble the Teacher any further?” Jesus overheard the message and spoke immediately to Jairus. “Do not be afraid; only believe.” He took Peter, James, and John with Him and continued to the house. When they arrived, the mourners were already wailing, the professional mourners hired for the funeral, along with the family’s weeping relatives. The death was confirmed. The ritual grief had begun. The matter was closed.

Jesus walked into the chaos and said something that made the mourners laugh at Him. “Why make this commotion and weep? The child is not dead, but sleeping.” They laughed Him to scorn. In their minds, He was in denial of a plain medical reality. Jesus did not argue. He simply put them all out of the room, the mourners, the professional wailers, the sceptics, and took only the parents and His three disciples with Him into the room where the girl lay. Then He did two things. He took her dead hand in His. And He spoke two Aramaic words to her. “Talitha, cumi.” Mark translates it for his Greek readers. “Little girl, I say to you, arise.” Immediately the twelve-year-old sat up. Mark adds the almost comic practical detail that Jesus then told them to give her something to eat. Death had been reversed in two words.

The Passion Translation renders the moment beautifully: “Jesus took her by the hand and said, ‘Talitha koum!’: ‘Little one, I say to you, arise and get up!’ Instantly the twelve-year-old girl stood up and walked around!” (Mark 5:41-42 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition captures the authority: “Gripping her [firmly] by the hand, He said to her, Talitha cumi,which translated is, Little girl, I say to you, arise (get up)! And instantly the girl got up and started walking around,for she was twelve years old” (Mark 5:41-42 AMPC). Instantly. The dead respond to the voice of Christ with no delay.

How Jesus Prayed

The Format. Jesus put out the unbelief first. Then He spoke directly to the dead girl. Two words. No long prayer. No religious preamble. A direct command addressed to the one who could no longer hear. The format teaches the believer that the atmosphere of unbelief must often be cleared before authority is exercised, and that the authority itself is often spoken in just a few words.

The Essence. Jesus related to the girl’s death the same way He related to sickness and storms. As something subordinate to His word. He called her, and she came back. The spiritual principle is that even death, in the Kingdom economy, is subordinate to the voice of the Son.

The Authority. The same Jesus who said “Talitha cumi” to Jairus’s daughter has given His disciples authority over sickness and even over death. Peter later raised Dorcas in Joppa by sending the mourners out of the room, kneeling, praying, and then saying, “Tabitha, arise” (Acts 9:40). Paul raised Eutychus from the dead in Troas (Acts 20:9-12). The authority flowed through His disciples because it had first flowed through them from Christ.

The Assurance. “The child is not dead, but sleeping.” Jesus spoke of the girl’s death as a sleep because for Him it was. He already knew what would happen. The assurance was total. There was no pleading, no hoping, no “if the Father is willing.” Jesus walked into the room already knowing the Father’s will on the matter.

The Submission. Jesus did not raise everyone who died in His three-year ministry. He raised specific ones for specific Kingdom purposes. The believer’s authority over sickness and death is always exercised in alignment with the Father’s purposes, not according to the believer’s preferences. Submission does not cancel the authority. Submission channels it.

The Result. A twelve-year-old girl walked out of her death bed and ate dinner with her parents. For Gospelbuzz readers today, wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, there may be a situation in your life that looks dead. A dream. A ministry. A relationship. A project. A vision the Father gave you years ago that seems to have breathed its last. Do not be afraid. Only believe. Clear the room of unbelief, take the situation by the hand, and speak the words Jesus taught His disciples to speak. Arise.

Prayer (Pattern After Jesus)

Address. Father, I thank You that the same Jesus who raised Jairus’s daughter is the Jesus who lives in me by His Spirit. Death and sickness are subordinate to His voice spoken through me.

Clear the Atmosphere. Today I put out of my prayer closet the mourners and the sceptics. I refuse to let the voices of unbelief fill the room. I take only the voice of the Father, the words of the Son, and the witness of the Spirit into this prayer.

Command. In the name of Jesus, I speak to [name the dead thing, the dream, the ministry, the relationship, the vision, the dying body]. Arise. Live. Be restored. By the authority of the One who raised the twelve-year-old, I call you back to Kingdom life.

Faith Declaration. I do not fear. I only believe. The dead thing is responding to the voice of Christ in me.

In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

The voice of Jesus living in me speaks to the dead things in my life and calls them back to life. I clear my atmosphere of unbelief. I take dead situations by the hand. I command them to arise, in Jesus’ name.
